Wind from WSW over ≈250 m of open water. Wave height and period follow the fetch-limited JONSWAP relations.

Hold ← → (or the buttons in the 3D view) to lean fully to one side. Lean out (right) before the corners to keep the line tight and avoid a jerk. Lean in (left) to reach the obstacles, but ride flat (lean ≈ 0°) up kickers and land flat: an edge on landing or a hit corner means a fall. Hold ↓ (Crouch) to absorb onto a box or on landing, and press ↑ (Pop) just before the kicker lip for a bigger jump. If your knees bottom out on a hard landing, you fall. Space pauses, . steps once.

Tricks. Hold Q (left) or R (right) on the kicker before the lip to pre-wind: the twist against the ramp starts the spin (≈0.4 s for a full wind-up). In the air, keep holding to add a little rotation through the line; the spin is otherwise fixed by angular momentum, and a grab tucks you and speeds it up. Hold W for a nose grab or S for a tail grab (in the air only; one hand leaves the handle, so the release limit drops to 60 %). Let go of the grab before touchdown and land within 40° of straight or switch; a 180 lands you switch. The buttons above Crouch/Pop do the same on touch screens.

Moves the load on the board. Trim, wetted length and centre of pressure follow from the moment balance: weight back lifts the nose and adds trim and drag; weight forward gives a long, flat contact.

The start jerk is set by momentum: the rider must go from 0 to cable speed (Δp ≈ m·Δv). Sliding: low carpet friction, but the full Δv. Jump: take-off just before the pull, so Δv is ≈2.6 m/s smaller. Sitting: deep squat, handle at the hips; rising to standing gives a long stroke that absorbs the jerk. In all three the arms and body yield above ≈0.95 kN.

If the line force stays above this limit for more than 30 ms, you lose the handle, which counts as a fall (as when you hit an obstacle). The warning level is 80 % of the limit.

Park layout · measured vs. assumed
TowerRolex (m)y (m)Status

Sources: cable loop from the user's Google Earth polygon (KML, perimeter 520 m); jetty, shore and obstacles from Google Earth screenshots (±2–3 m); satellite for the south and east (±15 m). x = east, y = north, origin at tower A. Direction of travel confirmed (counter-clockwise). Towers are leaning A-frames on the jetty/shore with a boom carrying the sheave 15–20 m out over the water. Obstacles move over time. The simulator uses layout O (Google Earth standard layer dated 6/9/2023) from the obstacle analysis of 25 Sep 2026: O1–O7 with their sub-contours and measured axes (O1 20.8 m, O2 19.6 m, O5 14.7 m, O7 21.2 m in Earth). Positions have ≈5–10 m absolute uncertainty. The unconfirmed dark candidate X1 is left out. The analysis gives no heights or product types, so types follow its planform reading (e.g. O3 kicker-like, O6 ramp section) and all heights are assumed typical values. The 2026 history layer (H1–H7) is not used. Contact physics: normal force, friction, jumps, landing and side collisions. Collisions with the jetty are not modelled.

Diagnostics (live) · report 13.7

All internal channels, so the simulator can be checked rather than just "look right": line tension, cable power, water-force components, wetted area, centre of pressure, dimensionless numbers, energy balance and contact state.

Physics from the report · validation

The model has been checked against the report section by section (1–19 and appendices). It follows "Physics and Simulation of a Cable-Park Wakeboard Rider" and sits between levels M2 and M3: rider and board with translation, yaw, roll, a reduced-coordinate multi-body rider (knees as two-link legs with torque limits, fore–aft body lean with ankle and hip balance strategies, arms that raise/lower and yield the handle, pose-dependent de Leva segment inertia), a unilateral line, one water-model function throughout, and a moving water surface (wind chop + own wake).

† Measured rope tension in a boat deep-water start (PMC case study; Runciman 2011 for slalom loads), not a cable-park measurement.

Start (instruction sources and model). Sitting start: elbows at the waist, handle at the hips, tense core, ~70 % weight on the back foot with the nose up; let the pull bring you up to standing (KiteSista; Miami Ski Nautique). Jump start: jump just before the line comes taut and land with bent knees and arms in (KiteSista). Measured deep-water start loads reach 2.0–2.5 × body weight (PMC case study). Headless model at 30 km/h, 80 kg: peak ≈1.43 kN sliding, ≈1.03 kN jump, ≈1.52 kN sitting (≈0.86–1.02 kN at 20 km/h).

Corner technique (instruction sources). Edge out before the corner, release the edge as the carrier goes round the sheave (~1 s of slack), and let the line pull you round. The HUD shows "Corner in … s".

Sources: the report above; de Leva (1996, segment inertia); knee-extension torque meta-analysis (Frontiers in Physiology 2021); Samozino et al. (jump force–velocity profiles); Horak & Nashner (1986, ankle/hip balance strategies); Hasselmann et al. (1973, JONSWAP); Rabaud & Moisy (2013) and Darmon, Benzaquen & Raphaël (2014, wake angle at high Froude number); Savitsky (1964) and NACA TN 4187 (1958); ITTC-1957; Tveitnes (2001, added mass); Runciman (2011) and Bray-Miners et al. (2013), slalom rope loads; IWWF Cable Wakeboard World Rules 2026; KiteSista and Wakeboarding Magazine, technique.
